name: Finazzi-Agrò PTNS versus sham
question: Does percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation improve urge incontinence after antimuscarinic failure compared with sham treatment?

design.population: 35 women with detrusor overactivity incontinence unresponsive to antimuscarinic therapy.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Purpose and Materials and Methods

verdictNote: Responder analysis excluded three randomized patients; the prespecified significance threshold was unavailable.
takeaway: Among women with detrusor overactivity incontinence after antimuscarinic failure who completed treatment, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation produced more patients with greater than 50% fewer urge-incontinence episodes than sham needle treatment (12/17 versus 0/15; P < 0.001).

reports.label: End-of-treatment randomized report
reports.citation: Finazzi-Agrò E, Petta F, Sciobica F, et al. "Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation Effects on Detrusor Overactivity Incontinence are Not Due to a Placebo Effect: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled Trial." *J Urol.* 2010;184(5):2001-2006. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.06.113
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

results.measure: More than 50% reduction in urge-incontinence episodes after treatment, among completers
results.note: The abstract defines response and reports P < 0.001 but does not identify a prespecified alpha threshold or explicitly label the endpoint primary.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

delivery.label: Treatment schedule and sham procedure
delivery.note: Sessions lasted 30 minutes, three times weekly in both groups.

delivery.label: Noncompletion unrelated to technique
delivery.note: The responder analysis included 17 PTNS and 15 sham completers.
